hubs.name: hub_business_entity
hubs.description: Company-wide party (business entity) register; persons share the same business entity number and therefore the same hub (one hub per business key). Integration point for sales, HR, purchasing and marketing. Email addresses and sign-in credentials attach via the same business entity number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source relations.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address identified by its own address number, shareable by several parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping), keyed on name per decided key.

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact types (role a person plays for an organisation), keyed on name per decided key.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type
hubs.description: Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile).

hubs.name: hub_country_region
hubs.description: Country or region identified by its ISO code.

hubs.name: hub_state_province
hubs.description: State or province reference list, keyed on name per decided key.

hubs.name: hub_department
hubs.description: Register of departments, the organisational units people work in, identified by department name.

hubs.name: hub_shift
hubs.description: Register of eight-hour working shifts, identified by shift name.

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates: people who applied for a position and whose application HR holds.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product, identified by its unique product number.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top-level merchandising category, identified by name.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Product subcategory, identified by name.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model, identified by name; several products can share one.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation, identified by its culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure, identified by short code.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description held in the description library.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Product photograph in the photo library.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (folder or document) in the controlled document library, identified by its hierarchy node.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory location, identified by name.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_work_order_operation
hubs.description: An operation within a work order, identified by work order and operation sequence.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason, identified by its failure description.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live store and the archive so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer review of a product.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: A purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_line
hubs.description: A line of a purchase order, identified by the purchase order together with its line number.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: A shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) for inbound purchases, identified by the shipping company name.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Party-address relationship: which address a party uses and in what capacity (address type). Many-to-many.

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Contact relationship: organisation (business entity), the person acting as its contact (role-qualified), and the contact type.

links.name: link_business_entity_phone_number_type
links.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type (PersonPhone).

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province an address sits in (country derived via the state).

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Department and shift assignment of an employee over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. An employee holds one department/shift assignment at a time.
links.unit_of_work: Employee (BusinessEntityID) + Department (Name) + Shift (Name), i.e. one assignment

links.name: link_job_candidate_business_entity
links.description: Links a job candidate to the employee they became when hired. Candidates without a link were not hired.

links.name: link_product_subcategory
links.description: Product placed in a subcategory (optional).

links.name: link_product_subcategory_category
links.description: Subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_product_model
links.description: Product belongs to at most one product model.

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture
links.description: Product model described by a product description in a specific culture.

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Many-to-many association of products and photographs.

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Illustrations supporting product models.

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Documents applying to products.

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner, an employee held in the existing HR area hub.

links.name: link_product_assembly_component
links.description: Bill of materials: assembly product (unqualified) built from a component product, quantity expressed in a unit of measure.

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory of a product held at a location.

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: Product being made by a work order.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order (optional).

links.name: link_work_order_operation
links.description: Operation of a work order, for a product, performed at a location.

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: Product involved in an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: Product to which a review relates.

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity_ship_method
links.description: Purchase order header relationships: the order is placed with exactly one vendor, created by one employee (buyer) and names one shipping method. Built from PurchaseOrderHeader (VendorID, EmployeeID, ShipMethodID).
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID with its VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID as recorded on the order header

links.name: link_purchase_order_line
links.description: A purchase order line belongs to its purchase order and refers to exactly one product (joined to the existing product hub via ProductID).
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the ProductID ordered on that line

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Vendor-product supply relationship (many-to-many) from ProductVendor, including the unit of measure in which the product is bought from that vendor.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + BusinessEntityID (vendor) pairing with its UnitMeasureCode

links.name: link_purchase_order_line_product
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTNUMBER; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity existence and last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person type and name details with full history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary name/contact data, separated from compliance-sensitive consent and sensitive demographics.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion preference (marketing consent) with history built by the warehouse.
satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive classification; history tracked separately.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Additional contact information and demographics (XML), access restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Sensitive data classification and XML data type; restricted separately from name reporting.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history of superseded values.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person); EmailAddress is declared as a feed of the hub.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change of a person's sign-in credential; hash and salt deliberately excluded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source (declared as a hub feed); credential values excluded from analytical use.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_numbers
satellites.description: Telephone numbers of a person per phone number type, with history.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship; history of relationships retained.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_contact_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the contact relationship; history retained.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details of an address with full history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic location (latitude/longitude) of an address.
satellites.split_rationale: Spatial data type and personal-data classification (geographic coordinates).

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type reference metadata.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type reference metadata.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, with history of renames.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name with visible rename history.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province ISO code and no-genuine-code flag.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, history preserved; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Different rate of change and business meaning (territory reassignment) from code/flag details.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_identifiers
satellites.description: Alternate employee identifiers: national ID number and network login. These are used to join data, not to anchor identity.
satellites.split_rationale: Identifier-type attributes; the national ID is sensitive, so these are kept apart from operational job data.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_job
satellites.description: Employment details: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly classification, active status and last-updated timestamp. History is built by observing overwrites.
satellites.split_rationale: Non-sensitive employment attributes that change slowly; this satellite holds the Employee ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_personal
satellites.description: Restricted personal employee data: date of birth, gender and marital status.
satellites.split_rationale: Data classification: personal data restricted to authorised HR users.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Point-in-time leave balance readings. Changes are captured as a series of balances.
satellites.split_rationale: Rate of change: leave balances change far more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and depth in the corporate reporting hierarchy. History is built by capturing changes.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes independently of job details and only its current value is held in the source.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Pay rate history per employee, keyed by effective rate change date: hourly rate and pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source relation at a finer grain (one row per rate change); EmployeePayHistory is declared as a feed of hub_business_entity.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department description: owning group and last change date. History is captured because the source overwrites it.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift definition: start and end time and last-updated timestamp. These can be adjusted over time.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. A missing EndDate marks the current assignment.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_details
satellites.description: Last-updated timestamp of each assignment record, one row per assignment start date.
satellites.split_rationale: Kept out of the effectivity satellite, which must carry exactly the start and end dates; multi-active on StartDate because repeated stints share the same link key.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé, held as a structured document, plus a last-updated timestamp.
satellites.split_rationale: Candidate personal data has its own retention and access rules.

satellites.name: sat_product_details
satellites.description: Descriptive and classification attributes of a product.
satellites.split_rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_pricing
satellites.description: Current standard cost and list price on the product record.
satellites.split_rationale: Financial figures change more frequently than descriptive attributes.

satellites.name: sat_product_inventory_policy
satellites.description: Inventory planning parameters.
satellites.split_rationale: Planning parameters maintained by supply chain at their own rate.

satellites.name: sat_product_lifecycle
satellites.description: Sale availability and discontinuation dates, plus record last-modified.
satellites.split_rationale: Lifecycle events change independently.

satellites.name: sat_product_cost_history
satellites.description: Standard cost history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (one row per cost period).

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price history periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (one row per price period).

satellites.name: sat_product_category_details
satellites.description: Category record currency.

satellites.name: sat_product_subcategory_details
satellites.description: Subcategory record currency.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_catalog
satellites.description: Structured catalogue information for publication.
satellites.split_rationale: Marketing-owned structured content.

satellites.name: sat_product_model_instructions
satellites.description: Structured manufacturing instructions.
satellites.split_rationale: Manufacturing-owned structured content.

satellites.name: sat_culture_details
satellites.description: Culture descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_unit_measure_details
satellites.description: Unit of measure descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_product_description_details
satellites.description: Marketing description text.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_thumbnail
satellites.description: Thumbnail image and file name.
satellites.split_rationale: Thumbnail version separate from large version.

satellites.name: sat_product_photo_large
satellites.description: Large image and file name.
satellites.split_rationale: Large version separate from thumbnail.

satellites.name: sat_product_product_photo_details
satellites.description: Principal-image flag for a product/photo association.

satellites.name: sat_illustration_details
satellites.description: Structured technical diagram.

satellites.name: sat_document_details
satellites.description: Document title, entry type, hierarchy depth, file type and summary.
satellites.split_rationale: Descriptive metadata.

satellites.name: sat_document_revision
satellites.description: Revision, engineering change number and approval status.
satellites.split_rationale: Revision control changes at a different rate.

satellites.name: sat_document_content
satellites.description: Full binary document content; inclusion to be confirmed.
satellites.split_rationale: Large binary data type isolated.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of a component in an assembly.

satellites.name: sat_product_assembly_component_details
satellites.description: Component quantity per assembly and BOM level, per BOM period start date.
satellites.split_rationale: BillOfMaterials is unique per assembly, component and start date; StartDate distinguishes concurrent rows.

satellites.name: sat_location_details
satellites.description: Hourly cost rate and capacity of a location.

satellites.name: sat_product_location_inventory
satellites.description: Quantity on hand per shelf and bin; captured over time by the vault.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_quantities
satellites.description: Ordered, stocked and scrapped quantities.
satellites.split_rationale: Output quantities separate from schedule.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_schedule
satellites.description: Work order start, end and due dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Schedule dates change independently of quantities.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_operation_schedule
satellites.description: Scheduled and actual operation dates.
satellites.split_rationale: Schedule vs cost concerns; WorkOrderRouting is unique per work order, product and sequence, so ProductID distinguishes rows.

satellites.name: sat_work_order_operation_cost
satellites.description: Resource hours and planned/actual cost of an operation.
satellites.split_rationale: Cost measures separate from schedule; ProductID distinguishes rows at WorkOrderRouting grain.

satellites.name: sat_scrap_reason_details
satellites.description: Scrap reason record currency.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_details
satellites.description: Live-store transaction details; order reference read with type.
satellites.split_rationale: Live source system.

satellites.name: sat_inventory_transaction_archive_details
satellites.description: Archived transaction details.
satellites.split_rationale: Archive source system.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_details
satellites.description: Review date, rating and comments.
satellites.split_rationale: Non-sensitive review content.

satellites.name: sat_product_review_reviewer_pii
satellites.description: Reviewer identity (personal data).
satellites.split_rationale: PII classification split for data protection.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_details
satellites.description: Vendor identification and descriptive details: account number, company name, optional purchasing web service address.
satellites.split_rationale: Slow-changing identifying/descriptive vendor attributes, separated from the status codes whose history is analysed.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_vendor_status
satellites.description: Vendor classification codes with history: credit rating, preferred status, active flag.
satellites.split_rationale: Coded status attributes whose change history must be retained and reconstructed at order time; carries the record's ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_status
satellites.description: Purchase order status and revision number, historised to trace status transitions and revisions.
satellites.split_rationale: Fast-changing workflow state, kept apart from dates and financial totals.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_dates
satellites.description: Order date and estimated shipment date of the purchase order.
satellites.split_rationale: Scheduling dates, largely static once set.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_totals
satellites.description: Order-level financial totals: subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Monetary amounts grouped together for spend analysis and reconciliation against lines.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_terms
satellites.description: Ordered quantity, unit price, line total and due date of the line.
satellites.split_rationale: Order terms set when the line is placed, changing rarely.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, historised to show receipt progression.
satellites.split_rationale: Running receipt figures that change with deliveries, split from the static order terms; carries ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Standing commercial supply terms: average lead time, standard price, min/max order quantities.
satellites.split_rationale: Agreed terms changing slowly, historised for trend analysis; separated from running values.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_running_values
satellites.description: Running values updated with activity: last receipt cost and date, quantity on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Fast-changing activity-driven figures, split from agreed terms by rate of change; carries ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_rates
satellites.description: Ship base and ship rate, historised so historical freight can be assessed against rates in force.
satellites.split_rationale: Changing rate terms; rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning (REQ-077).

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_identifiers
satellites.description: Internal shipping method identifier used on purchase orders.
satellites.split_rationale: Static internal identifier, separated from changing rates.

evidence: Customer.AccountNumber is 'number identifying the customer assigned by the accounting system'. No customer hub exists in the vault, and no existing hub has a matching business key.
Customer.CustomerID is the primary key of Customer. The vault has no customer hub.
Customer has its own surrogate key. PersonID and StoreID are only foreign keys to other concepts.
Store.BusinessEntityID is an int primary key with the same name and format as hub_business_entity's key BusinessEntityID.
Person, Employee and Vendor already feed hub_business_entity with this key, so Store looks like another BusinessEntity subtype.
The column comment says 'Foreign key to Customer.BusinessEntityID', but Customer has no such column. That comment is unreliable, and no explicit cross-reference to BusinessEntity is given.
SalesOrderNumber is a computed identifier of the sales order. The vault has no sales order hub.
hub_purchase_order is keyed on PurchaseOrderID, a different concept (purchasing, not selling).
SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderID is the primary key of the sales order. No sales order hub exists.
hub_purchase_order is a different business concept.
SalesOrderDetail is a sales order line. The only line hub in the vault is hub_purchase_order_line, which is for purchasing and is a different concept.
SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID comment: 'Foreign key to Employee.BusinessEntityID'.
Employee already feeds hub_business_entity under the BusinessEntityID key, so this is the same key.
SalesTerritory.TerritoryID is the primary key of a sales territory lookup. No territory hub exists.
hub_state_province has a sat 'territory', but that is an attribute and not a territory hub.
SalesTerritory.Name is the territory description, an alternate key. No sales territory hub exists, and the other hubs keyed on Name are unrelated concepts.
CreditCard.CreditCardID is the primary key of credit card records. Nothing in the vault models credit cards.
CardNumber is a candidate key of the credit card. There is no existing credit card hub, so it belongs to a new one.
Currency.CurrencyCode is the ISO currency code and the primary key of the Currency lookup. No currency hub exists.
hub_country_region is keyed on CountryRegionCode, a different key. CountryRegionCurrency only links the two.
CurrencyRate.CurrencyRateID is the surrogate primary key of exchange rates. No existing construct models it.
This is the natural composite key of the exchange rate (date plus from and to currency). No existing hub models exchange rates.
SpecialOffer.SpecialOfferID is the primary key of a discount lookup. The vault has no promotion or discount hub.
SalesReason.SalesReasonID is the primary key of the lookup of customer purchase reasons. Nothing similar exists in the vault.
hub_scrap_reason is a manufacturing concept and unrelated.
ShoppingCartItem holds online cart items until an order is submitted. No shopping cart construct exists in the vault.
SalesTaxRate.SalesTaxRateID is the primary key of the tax rate lookup. No tax rate hub exists.
StateProvinceID is only a foreign key to state/province.
Person is already listed in hub_business_entity's fed_by, and the key BusinessEntityID is identical.

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify every customer by the customer account number assigned by the accounting system.
The customer account number uniquely identifies a customer.
The business must be able to distinguish an individual-person customer from a store customer.
For an individual customer, the business must retain the reference to the person who is the customer.
For a store customer, the business must retain the reference to the store.
The business must know the sales territory in which each customer is located.
Every customer is assigned an account number by the accounting system and is located in a sales territory.
A customer is either an individual person or a reseller store (to be confirmed with sales operations, see C-02).
The business must know when a customer's record was last changed in the operating system, so that reporting can be reconciled against the source.
The business must be able to report the customer base by territory and by customer kind (individual vs. store).
The business must be able to identify each store by its business entity reference.
The business must record the store name of each store.
The business must know which sales representative is assigned to each store.
The business must retain the store demographics captured for each store, covering number of employees, annual sales and store type.
The business must be able to segment reseller performance by store demographic characteristics such as store size or store type.
The business must identify every sales order by its unique sales order number.
The business must know which customer placed each order.
The business must know whether an order was placed online by the customer or entered by a sales representative, as this distinguishes the two sales channels.
For orders that were not placed online, the business must know which sales representative created the order.
The business must know the territory in which each sale was made, recorded on the order itself.
The order territory is held separately from the customer's territory and the representative's current territory, and reporting must be explicit about which territory is meant.
The business must track the order creation date, the date the order is due to the customer, and the date it was shipped.
The business must track the current status of an order.
The allowed order status values are in process, approved, backordered, rejected, shipped and cancelled.
The business must be able to measure order fulfilment performance, i.e. whether orders shipped on or before their due date.
The business must retain the customer's own purchase order number where the customer supplied one.
The business must retain the financial accounting number reference carried on the order, to allow reconciliation with finance.
The business must know the billing address used for each order.
The business must know the shipping address used for each order, separately from the billing address.
The business must know the shipping method chosen for each order.
The business must retain sales representative comments recorded against an order, as context for enquiries and disputes.
The business must be able to report order counts and values by channel, by territory, by representative, by customer and by period.
The business must track the revision number of an order, an incremental number tracking changes to the order over time, so it can tell that an order has been amended and how many times.
The business must record the order subtotal, the sum of the line totals for the order.
The business must record the tax amount charged on the order.
The business must record the freight (shipping cost) charged on the order.
The business must record the total due from the customer, described as subtotal plus tax plus freight.
The business must be able to analyse revenue with tax and freight separated from product revenue.
The business must know which credit card was used to pay for an order, where a card was used.
The business must retain the credit card approval code provided by the card company, for payment reconciliation and dispute handling.
The business must be able to report the share of orders paid by card versus those with no card recorded.
requirements.obj: share of orders paid by card

requirements.text: The business must know which currency exchange rate was applied to each order where the order was not in the company's base currency.
The business must be able to report sales both in the transaction currency and converted to a reporting currency, using the rate that applied to the order.
requirements.obj: sales in transaction and reporting currency

requirements.text: Each order is made up of one or more order lines.
The business must identify each order line within its order, using one incremental unique number per product sold.
The business must know which product was sold on each order line.
The business must know the quantity ordered per product on each line.
The business must know the unit selling price of the product on each line.
The business must know the discount amount applied to each line.
The business must know the line total, described as unit price × (1 − discount) × quantity.
The business must know which special offer (promotional code) applied to each line, so that promotional effectiveness can be measured.
The business must retain the shipment tracking number supplied by the shipper for each line, because lines of one order may ship separately.
The business must be able to analyse sales by product, by quantity, by realised price and by discount level.
The business must be able to distinguish list-price revenue from discount given away, at line level.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales reasons, each with a description and a reason category.
The business must know which sales reasons were recorded against each order.
An order may have several sales reasons, and a sales reason may apply to many orders.
The business must be able to report order volume and value by sales reason and by reason category.
requirements.obj: order volume and value by sales reason

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the proportion of orders for which no sales reason was recorded, as a data-quality measure.
requirements.obj: proportion of orders without sales reason

requirements.text: The business must identify each sales representative by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference.
The business must know the territory a representative is currently assigned to.
The business must know each representative's projected yearly sales quota.
The business must know the bonus due if the quota is met.
The business must know the commission percentage a representative receives per sale.
The business must know each representative's year-to-date sales total and previous-year sales total as maintained by the operational system.
The business must be able to compare a representative's actual sales against quota and identify who is on track to earn the bonus.
The business must be able to report sales by representative over time, independently of the running totals held in the operational system.
The business must maintain the catalogue of sales territories, each with a territory name.
The business must know the country or region each territory belongs to.
The business must know the geographic group a territory belongs to, so that results can be rolled up regionally.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date sales and previous-year sales.
The business must know each territory's year-to-date business costs and previous-year costs.
The business must be able to report territory contribution, sales against costs, for the current and previous year.
The business must be able to roll territory results up to geographic group and to country/region.
The business must maintain the register of credit cards used for payment, identified by the card record held in the operational system.
The business must know the card type (card name), the card number, and the expiry month and year of each credit card.
The business must be able to report sales by card type.
Credit card numbers and expiry data are sensitive personal and payment information, and access to them must be restricted.
The business must state whether the card number is needed at all in the warehouse or whether a masked or partial value is sufficient.
The business must know which credit cards belong to which person.
A person may hold several credit cards, and a card may be associated with more than one person.
The business must be able to identify cards used on orders that are not registered to the ordering customer, as an input to fraud and data-quality review.
requirements.obj: cards used on orders not registered to the ordering customer

requirements.text: References to product, person/business entity, employee, address, shipping method and country/region/state/province data maintained outside the sales area must be preserved so sales information can later be joined to those areas.
The business must record the sales tax rates by state/province and transaction type.
The business must record special offers and discounts and which products they apply to.
The business must record currencies, currency exchange rates and the currencies in which each country/region trades.
The business must record online shopping cart activity.
The business needs a consolidated, historical view of sales activity for reporting, performance management and planning.
The business must retain shopping cart items, each identified within its shopping cart.
The business must know the shopping cart identifier for each cart item.
requirements.obj: shopping cart identifier of cart item

requirements.text: The business must know the product for each cart item.
The business must know the quantity ordered for each cart item.
The business must know the date and time each cart item was created.
requirements.obj: creation date and time of cart item

requirements.text: The business must be able to report which products are added to carts, and in what quantities.
requirements.obj: products added to carts and their quantities

requirements.text: The business must be able to measure cart activity over time, using the creation date of cart items.
The business must maintain the catalogue of special offers, each with a discount description.
The business must know each special offer's discount percentage.
The business must know each special offer's discount type category.
requirements.obj: discount type category of special offer

requirements.text: The business must know the group the discount applies to (for example Reseller or Customer), so that promotions can be reported per channel.
The business must know each special offer's minimum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's maximum quantity threshold.
The business must know each special offer's start date, as the beginning of the period during which it is valid.
The business must know each special offer's end date, as the end of the period during which it is valid.
The business must be able to determine which special offers were valid at any given date, including offers that have since expired, so that historical orders can be explained.
requirements.obj: special offers valid at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each special offer.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per special offer

requirements.text: The business must be able to report revenue and discount attributable to each offer type and category.
requirements.obj: revenue and discount per offer type and category

requirements.text: The business must know which products each special offer applies to.
requirements.obj: products covered by each special offer

requirements.text: An offer may cover many products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
The business must be able to check that the offer recorded on an order line was applicable to the product on that line, as a data-quality and pricing-governance control.
requirements.obj: applicability of order line offer to order line product

requirements.text: The business must maintain the list of currencies, identified by their ISO currency code, with the currency name.
The business must be able to present currency names in reporting rather than raw codes.
The business must retain exchange rates as a time series, recording for each rate the date and time the rate was obtained.
requirements.obj: exchange rate with date and time obtained

requirements.text: The business must record for each exchange rate the currency converted from and the currency converted to.
requirements.obj: source and target currency of exchange rate

requirements.text: The business must retain the average exchange rate for the day.
requirements.obj: average exchange rate for the day

requirements.text: The business must retain the final (end-of-day) exchange rate, as it serves a different reporting purpose from the average rate.
The business must be able to reproduce the exchange rate actually applied to a given order, not merely today's rate, so that historical reporting is stable and does not change when rates move.
requirements.obj: exchange rate applied to an order

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the same sales figures in more than one currency.
The business must state which of the two rates (average or end-of-day) is used for each currency report.
requirements.obj: rate type used for each report

requirements.text: The business must be able to identify orders where no exchange rate was recorded and understand how those are to be treated (presumed base currency).
requirements.obj: orders without a recorded exchange rate

requirements.text: The business must know which currencies are used in which countries/regions.
A country/region may be associated with more than one currency, and a currency with more than one country/region.
The business must be able to check that sales in a given country/region were transacted in a currency valid for that country/region.
requirements.obj: validity of sales currency for country/region

requirements.text: The business must maintain the register of sales tax rates, each with a tax rate description.
The business must know the state, province or country/region each tax rate applies to.
The business must know the tax type for each rate, using the operational meanings: applied to retail transactions, applied to wholesale transactions, or applied to all sales.
The business must know the tax rate amount.
The business must be able to report tax collected by jurisdiction and by tax type.
requirements.obj: tax collected by jurisdiction and tax type

requirements.text: The business must be able to compare the tax amount charged on an order with the tax rates applicable to the relevant jurisdiction, as a compliance check.
requirements.obj: order tax amount with applicable tax rates

requirements.text: A sales order is placed by exactly one customer.
A customer may place many orders over time.
A sales order is handled by at most one sales representative.
Orders placed online by the customer have no sales representative.
A sales representative handles many orders.
A sales order is made in one sales territory, and a territory carries many orders.
A sales order consists of one or more order lines, and each order line belongs to exactly one order.
An order line sells one product, and a product is sold on many order lines.
An order line may be sold under one special offer, and an offer is used on many order lines.
A sales order may cite several sales reasons, and a sales reason may be cited on many orders.
A sales order may be paid with one credit card, and a card may be used on many orders.
A credit card may be registered to one or more people, and a person may hold several cards.
A sales order may use one currency exchange rate, and a rate may apply to many orders.
A customer is located in one sales territory, and a territory contains many customers.
A customer is either a person or a store.
A reseller store is served by one sales representative, and a representative serves many stores.
A sales representative is currently assigned to at most one territory.
A sales representative has worked a series of territories over time.
A sales territory belongs to one country/region and to one geographic group.
A special offer applies to one or more products, and a product may be covered by several offers.
A country/region may trade in several currencies, and a currency may be used in several countries/regions.
An exchange rate converts from one currency to another on a given day.
A sales tax rate applies to one state/province or country/region for a given tax type.
A shopping cart contains one or more cart items, each for one product.
There is no recorded link from a shopping cart to a customer or to an order.
A sales order carries a billing address and a shipping address, which may differ.
A sales order is shipped using one shipping method.
The business must retain the full history of sales quotas per sales representative, including the quota date and the quota amount in force from that date.
The business must be able to determine the quota that applied to a representative at any point in the past and compare it to the sales actually achieved in that period.
The business must be able to report how a representative's quota has moved over time and how often it was revised.
The representative record also carries a single current quota figure alongside the dated quota history.
Reporting must state whether it uses the current quota figure or the dated quota history, and the two must be reconcilable.
The business must retain the history of which representative worked which territory, with the date the representative started work in the territory and the date they left.
A representative's territory assignment is open-ended, with no end date recorded, while the representative is still working the territory.
The business must be able to identify the currently active territory assignment for each representative.
The business must be able to determine who was responsible for a territory on any given date, so that historical sales can be credited to the person who actually held the territory at the time.
requirements.obj: responsible representative for territory at a date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see the sequence of representatives who have held a territory and how long each held it.
requirements.obj: sequence and duration of representatives per territory

requirements.text: The representative record also carries the territory currently assigned alongside the dated assignment history, the same current-versus-historical duality as the quota.
Where an order's territory differs from the representative's territory at the time of the order, the business must be able to see and explain that difference.
requirements.obj: difference between order territory and representative territory

requirements.text: Exchange rates are a daily time series, and the business needs the rate as at the relevant date.
Exchange rates must never be retrospectively overwritten in reporting.
Special offers have explicit start and end dates.
The business must be able to determine the special offers that were live at any date, including expired ones.
requirements.obj: special offers live at a date

requirements.text: The business must be able to see how descriptive information changes over time where it matters commercially, in particular a customer's territory, a store's assigned representative, a store's demographics, a special offer's discount percentage, and a territory's group.
requirements.obj: changes in descriptive information over time

requirements.text: Every record in this area carries a last modified date and time, which the business needs as the primary signal that something has changed.
The business needs the last modified date and time as the basis for reconciling warehouse content with the operational system.
For all other entities in this area, the operational system holds only the current state, so history can only be built from the point the warehouse starts capturing it.
The business must decide for which of the other entities capturing history is worth doing.
requirements.obj: entities for which history is captured

requirements.text: Report sales value and volume by period, territory, geographic group, country/region, representative, customer, customer kind, product, channel, currency, special offer and sales reason.
Compare actual sales against quota per representative and per period, including the bonus and commission implications.
Report territory profitability using sales and cost figures at territory level.
Measure discounting: total discount given, by offer, by product, by channel and by customer kind.
Measure fulfilment: order-to-ship elapsed time, on-time-against-due-date performance, and the distribution of order statuses.
Measure channel mix: online orders versus representative-entered orders, in volume and value.
Report tax and freight separately from product revenue.
Report sales in a single reporting currency across all territories, using the rate that applied to each order.
Analyse the reseller base by store demographics and by assigned representative.
Analyse online cart activity by product and period, within the limits noted in C-10.

The business must be able to see, for each order, whether the key commercial attributes are present: customer, territory, representative (where not online), currency rate (where non-base currency), and payment reference.
requirements.obj: presence of key commercial attributes on orders

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that the order total agrees with the sum of its lines plus tax and freight, and to report where it does not.
requirements.obj: order total against lines, tax and freight

requirements.text: The business must be able to check that line totals agree with quantity, unit price and discount as described by the source.
The business must be able to report orders referencing a special offer that is outside its validity period at the order date.
The business must be able to report customers that are neither a person nor a store, or that are both, once C-02 is resolved.
requirements.obj: customers that are neither or both person and store

requirements.text: The business must be able to report representatives with no territory, and territories with no representative, on any given date.
requirements.obj: representatives without territory and territories without representative

requirements.text: The business must be able to reconcile operationally maintained running totals (representative and territory year-to-date and last-year figures) against totals recalculated from orders, and to report material differences.
requirements.obj: running totals against recalculated order totals

requirements.text: Each entity in this area has a named business owner who is accountable for its definitions and for resolving the clarifications in this document.
Business owners for the entities must be assigned before the warehouse is built.
Credit card data (card number, expiry, card type, holder association) is payment-sensitive, and its handling, retention and access rules must be defined before it is loaded.
Individual customers are natural persons.
Personal-data handling rules, including retention limits and the treatment of deletion requests, must be defined for the customer information in this area.
Sales representative quota, bonus, commission and achievement figures are remuneration data about identifiable individuals and must be access-restricted to those with a legitimate need.
Store demographics are commercially sensitive information about reseller partners and must be treated as confidential.
The replication identifier carried by several records has no business meaning and is not required by the business, but may be retained as a technical trace of the source record.
Values computed by the operational system (order number, customer account number, line total, order subtotal and total due) are to be taken as given from the source rather than recalculated.
Values computed by the operational system must be checkable.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-001 states every customer is identified by the account number assigned by the accounting system, and REQ-002 states it uniquely identifies a customer. REQ-007 says every customer has one (not nullable), and REQ-047-3 says it is taken as given from the source.
System-generated surrogate in the Customer source. The requirements do not call it a business identifier, so it is a weak key. It is only a fallback if AccountNumber proves unreliable.
REQ-011 states each store is identified by its business entity reference. It is stable, recognised by the business and carried on every store (REQ-012, REQ-013).
REQ-016 states every sales order is identified by its unique sales order number. REQ-047-3 notes the source computes it. It is unique and non-null.
System-generated surrogate for the order header, used as the source key and referenced by order lines and sales reasons. It is weak as a business key. The requirements prefer the sales order number.

REQ-045 says an order line is identified within its order by one incremental unique number. It is only unique together with the parent order (SalesOrderID or SalesOrderNumber), so it forms a composite key. Taken alone it is a weak key.
REQ-060 states each sales representative is identified by their business entity reference, which is also their employee reference. It is stable, unique and recognised by the business.

The requirements (REQ-068 to REQ-070) describe a territory catalogue with a territory name but give no explicit identifier. TerritoryID is the source key referenced by customers, orders and representatives (REQ-006, REQ-020, REQ-061). It is a system-assigned id, so the score is moderate.
REQ-068 says each territory has a name. The requirements do not state that the name is unique or immutable, so it is a weaker alternative.

REQ-075 says cards are identified by the card record held in the operational system. This is the only identifier the requirements give, although it is system-generated. CardNumber is sensitive (REQ-078, REQ-079) and is not preferred.

REQ-076 says the business knows the card number, so it identifies a card. REQ-078, REQ-079 and REQ-041-3 restrict it as sensitive data and question whether it is needed at all. It is therefore a poor key candidate.
REQ-022-2 states currencies are identified by their ISO currency code. It is stable, unique and recognised by the business.

System-generated source id for an exchange rate. REQ-024-2 and REQ-025-2 suggest a natural composite of rate date, FromCurrencyCode and ToCurrencyCode (REQ-062-2: one currency to another on a given day). This id is a weak surrogate.

REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2 and REQ-062-2 describe an exchange rate as converting from one currency to another on a given date. The combination is the natural business identity, but the requirements do not explicitly call it unique.
The requirements (REQ-008-2, REQ-051) refer to the special offer or promotional code but give no explicit identifier. SpecialOfferID is the only source key, and it is system-assigned.

REQ-055 describes a sales reason catalogue with a description and a reason category, and REQ-056 links reasons to orders. No natural identifier is stated, so the source key is used. The name is a possible alternative but is not stated to be unique.

REQ-001-2 says cart items are each identified within their shopping cart, and REQ-002-2 says the cart identifier is known. The cart identifier plus the item id gives a composite key. ShoppingCartItemID alone is a surrogate.

REQ-035-2 describes a tax rate register. REQ-063-2 says a rate applies to one state/province for a tax type, which suggests a natural composite of StateProvinceID and TaxType. SalesTaxRateID is a system-assigned source key.

REQ-004 and REQ-080 require the reference to the person who is a customer or holds a credit card. REQ-083 requires preserving person/business entity references. It is the source reference, but person data is maintained outside this area.

hubs.description: Company-wide party (business entity) register; persons share the same business entity number and therefore the same hub (one hub per business key). Integration point for sales, HR, purchasing and marketing. Email addresses and sign-in credentials attach via the same business entity number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source relations.

hubs.name: hub_sales_tax_rate
hubs.description: Sales tax rate from the tax rate register.
